THE SKY APPEARS BLUE DURING THE DAY DUE TO RAYLEIGH SCATTERING, WHICH IS THE SCATTERING OF LIGHT BY PARTICLES MUCH SMALLER THAN ITS WAVELENGTH. SUNLIGHT CONSISTS OF MULTIPLE WAVELENGTHS, WITH SHORTER WAVELENGTHS (BLUE/VIOLET) SCATTERED MORE EFFICIENTLY THAN LONGER ONES (RED/ORANGE). OUR EYES ARE MORE SENSITIVE TO BLUE LIGHT, AND VIOLET IS LESS PERCEIVED, SO THE SKY SEEMS BLUE.

AT SUNSET, THE SUN'S LIGHT TRAVELS THROUGH MORE ATMOSPHERE, INCREASING THE PATH LENGTH. THIS CAUSES MOST OF THE SHORTER WAVELENGTHS (BLUE) TO BE SCATTERED OUT OF THE DIRECT PATH. ONLY THE LONGER WAVELENGTHS (RED/ORANGE) REMAIN, MAKING THE SUN AND SKY APPEAR RED. RAYLEIGH SCATTERING'S INVERSE FOURTH-POWER RELATIONSHIP WITH WAVELENGTH EXPLAINS THIS PHENOMENON.
